opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max access is write (admin only if role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists Karen Alexander (E030) as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read unless advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: HR's database (system of record for employment type) lists Karen Alexander (E030) as a full-time Analyst. Under policy, full-time employees may have up to write, and admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code (Engineer does), so the maximum is write. The requested write access equals the maximum, so write is granted. The Security note's contractor classification conflicts with HR's verified employment record, but I treat HR as authoritative for employment type.
